summary: Nvidia has unveiled a prototype of its next-generation co-packaged optics (CPO) technology, Optics-on-Interposer (OOI), at SEMICON West 2026. summary: DeepSeek and MiniMax have received approval to deploy their artificial intelligence models overseas, according to a post published October 22 by China Central Television’s Yuyuantantan account. summary: South Korean image-sensing module maker Namuga is accelerating its physical AI strategy after securing a supply deal with a global humanoid robot company. title: Chinese automakers capture record 14.6% Europe market share as looming hybrid import curbs spur shipments
summary: Chinese automakers achieved record sales in Europe in September, doubling their monthly volume to 194,800 vehicles and capturing an unprecedented 14.6% market share. Beyond their expanding model portfolios, the surge appears to reflect accelerated shipments ahead of potential European Union restrictions on Chinese hybrid vehicle imports, expected to take effect in 2027.

title: AI data centers drive Taiwan's electrical firms into modular, EPC markets
summary: As demand for AI data centers expands, next-generation AI servers are raising requirements for power supply, cooling efficiency, and deployment speed. Taiwan's electrical and mechanical equipment providers are therefore moving beyond standalone equipment supply into system integration, engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC), and modular data center solutions.

title: Meta’s AI commitments surge to US$825 billion, testing financing power
summary: Meta Platforms’ long-term AI infrastructure spending is driving rising financial pressure, with free cash flow turning negative in Q3 2026 and future lease and non-cancelable contract commitments climbing to about US$825 billion. The company also raised the lower end of its 2026 capex forecast by US$5 billion to US$135 billion, signaling continued AI expansion as financing and investment returns become new challenges.

title: Texas Instruments sees up to $1,000 in chip content per humanoid robot as analog supply tightens
summary: Texas Instruments (TI) held its latest earnings call this week, projecting fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of US$5.8 billion to US$6.3 billion. The midpoint of its guidance is broadly in line with third-quarter revenue, outperforming the seasonal declines typically seen in the fourth quarter.

title: Column: Will general-purpose models overtake Physical AI?
summary: After GPT-6 Astra launched in early September 2026, researchers quickly put it through Physical AI and robotics benchmarks. In some tests, it outperformed specialized models trained on large amounts of robot data.

summary: Magnate Technology expects rising aircraft engine demand and semiconductor equipment opportunities to support growth as it expands production capacity, with implications for global aviation and chip supply chains. title: Moonshot's Singapore hiring shows how China's open-model labs plan to get paid abroad
summary: Moonshot AI's first visible overseas sales hire marks a new stage in how Chinese developers of open-weight models compete outside China. title: Tesla-SpaceX merger tests whether Musk's technology empire is worth more together
summary: Since Elon Musk publicly confirmed that Tesla and SpaceX are evaluating a potential merger, the prospect has stirred widespread speculation over what could become the largest corporate transaction in history—and whether combining two of Musk's biggest technology platforms would actually create value beyond the sprawling ecosystem they already share.

title: Interview: The story of LEACHIM, a working humanoid robot from the 1970s
summary: The robotics industry has come a long way since robots were first built over 50 years ago. title: Nvidia rejects near-term memory glut fears, leaves CXMT cooperation open
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company did not expect memory supply to exceed demand in the coming years and remained open to working with China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). title: SpaceX's 80,000-site push turns Starlink from satellite overlay into full mobile challenger
summary: SpaceX has firmly established itself in direct-to-device connectivity through Starlink's expanding satellite constellation. But the space giant is now pushing beyond orbital coverage as it seeks an equally consequential position in terrestrial mobile infrastructure.

title: Bosch to spin off automotive business as Asian rivals intensify pressure
summary: Bosch Group plans to establish Bosch Mobility as a wholly owned, legally independent subsidiary in August 2027, separating the business that generated about 60% of group revenue. The move will complete the restructuring of Bosch's four major business areas and leave the parent company focused on strategic oversight and centralized research and development.

title: AIDC launches Taiwan's largest industrial microgrid with 9MW/54MWh energy storage capacity
summary: Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) held an inauguration ceremony for its 9MW/54MWh large-scale microgrid system at its Shuinan facility in Taichung on October 22, marking the official commissioning of what the company describes as Taiwan's largest industrial behind-the-meter energy storage microgrid.

title: LGES Poland plant nears breakeven as utilization rebounds
summary: LG Energy Solution (LGES)'s Wroclaw plant in Poland, long viewed as a major drag on the business, is nearing profitability after posting an operating loss of nearly KRW600 billion (approximately US$430 million) in 2025. A surge in European EV demand and the early conversion of some production lines to energy storage system (ESS) applications have lifted utilization, putting the plant on track to return to profit in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: Doosan Robotics targets automakers, chipmakers as Chinese rivals cut prices
summary: Doosan Robotics is focusing its sales efforts on large automotive and semiconductor manufacturers as it develops AI-powered systems capable of handling more complex factory tasks, Hyeonchang Jeon, senior manager of the company's Korea sales team, said in an interview with DIGITIMES at FIX 2026 in Daegu, South Korea.

title: Taiwan's inaugural semiconductor strike pauses as nearly 70% of Micron Taoyuan Union rejects new bonus offer
summary: Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry has temporarily drawn to a close. A 24-hour warning strike spearheaded by Micron Technology's Taoyuan union concluded on the morning of October 23, 2026. Formal labor-management negotiations are set to resume on October 27.
